findings.title: float: right on .small-action button is ignored once .small-action becomes a flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex`, which makes its direct children flex items. The CSS spec says `float` has no effect on flex items, so `button { float: right; }` (and `.topic-avatar { float: left; }`) no longer does anything. The action button (edit/delete on small-action posts) will now sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` instead of being pushed to the right edge, a visible layout regression. To keep the previous placement the button needs `margin-left: auto` (as was done for `.panel` in header.scss), and the dead `float` declarations should be removed.

findings.title: margin-left: auto does not right-align in legacy -webkit-box / -moz-box flex implementations
findings.body: `.panel` was changed from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto` to push it to the right of the flex row. The `flexbox()` mixin deliberately emits `display: -webkit-box` / `display: -moz-box` for old engines (Android stock browser ≤4.3, Safari ≤6, Firefox ≤21), but those 2009-syntax implementations do not honour `margin: auto` on box children. In exactly the browsers the mixin is trying to support, the header panel (search/hamburger/user icons) will now sit immediately after the title instead of at the right edge, whereas the old `float: right` worked everywhere. Either accept that and drop the legacy prefixes, or add a flexible spacer / `-webkit-box-flex` on the title.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits non-existent -ms-align-items and relies on value names that differ in legacy specs
findings.body: `-ms-align-items` is not a property any version of IE ever implemented (IE10 uses `-ms-flex-align`, IE11 uses unprefixed `align-items`), so that line is dead output. Additionally the legacy `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` properties use `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`; the mixin passes `$alignment` through unchanged, so any future call with `flex-start`/`flex-end` will silently produce invalid declarations for those engines. Current call sites only use `center` and `baseline`, which happen to be shared, but the mixin as written is misleading.

findings.title: order mixin maps 0-based `order` directly onto 1-based -webkit-box-ordinal-group
findings.body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (2009 flexbox) is 1-based with a default of 1, while standard `order` is 0-based with a default of 0. Passing the same value to both means an element given `order(1)` would be placed at the same position as un-ordered siblings in legacy WebKit rather than after them. Current usages (2 and 3) happen to preserve relative ordering, but the mixin will produce inconsistent results across engines for other values; either offset the legacy value by 1 or drop the legacy prefix.

findings.title: PR title/description do not describe the change; .valign-helper left as a now-meaningless flex item
findings.body: The PR is titled as a header performance optimisation and the description is just "Test 5", but the change is actually a layout rewrite from floats to flexbox across header, topic, small-action posts and badges with visible behavioural differences. Reviewers and future readers of history cannot tell what was intended. Related leftover: `.valign-helper` (inline-block, height 100%, vertical-align middle) existed solely to vertically centre floated siblings; with `.contents` now using `align-items: center` it becomes an empty flex item and should be removed along with the markup that renders it.
